description: Clinical and epidemiological inputs used by the simulation. Numerical values are unchanged; metadata records their provenance or assumption status.
reference: See each input group's reference and the source/doi fields on individual ABR estimates.

epidemiology.description: Bleeding-event allocation, annual ICH incidence, and event-specific case-fatality inputs.
reference: World Federation of Hemophilia. World Bleeding Disorders Registry 2023 Data Report. https://www1.wfh.org/publications/files/pdf-2452.pdf
Andersson NG et al. Br J Haematol. 2017. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjh.14844

event_fractions.description: AJBR fraction allocates total bleeds to joint bleeds. The non-ICH value is a proxy based on uncommon major anatomical bleeding sites, not a directly observed all-site probability.
reference: AJBR fraction: existing project assumption; original source is not documented and must be verified.
Non-ICH proxy: WFH World Bleeding Disorders Registry 2023 Data Report. https://www1.wfh.org/publications/files/pdf-2452.pdf
Supporting iliopsoas evidence: WFH World Bleeding Disorders Registry 2018 Data Report. https://elearning.wfh.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/WBDR_2018_Data_Report_EN.pdf

event_rates.description: Annual ICH incidence rates by treatment regime; the model converts these rates to cycle probabilities.
event_rates.reference: Andersson NG et al. Br J Haematol. 2017. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjh.14844

intracranial_hemorrhage_rate.description: Central annual ICH-rate inputs. Verify the final numerator and person-time extraction when locking the calibration.
reference: Andersson NG et al. Br J Haematol. 2017. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjh.14844

epidemiology.ich_case_fatality_description: Death conditional on ICH. The central value is approximately consistent with 2 deaths among 24 reported ICH events; uncertainty should be sampled in PSA.
epidemiology.ich_case_fatality_reference: Andersson NG et al. Br J Haematol. 2017. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjh.14844
epidemiology.non_ich_case_fatality_description: Structural base-case assumption of no immediate fatality from the aggregated non-ICH major-bleeding proxy; this is not a published estimate.
epidemiology.non_ich_case_fatality_reference: Modeling assumption caused by insufficient subtype-specific evidence; vary in sensitivity analysis.

utilities.description: Treatment-regime-specific utility decrements retained from the existing model.
utilities.reference: Existing project assumption; primary published source and time-unit derivation require verification.

decrements.description: Utility decrement by treatment regime, interpreted using the time unit implemented in the calculation code.
decrements.reference: Existing project calibration; source is not documented in the repository.

clinical_scoring.description: Rules translating accumulated treated joint bleeding into Pettersson-score progression and severity. The model adds one Pettersson point per 12.6 hemarthrosis events.
reference: Zhou ZY, Raimundo K, Patel AM, et al. Model of Short- and Long-Term Outcomes of Emicizumab Prophylaxis Treatment for Persons with Hemophilia A. J Manag Care Spec Pharm. 2020;26(9):1109-1120. https://doi.org/10.18553/jmcp.2020.19406

Fischer K, van Hout BA, van der Bom JG, et al. Association between joint bleeds and Pettersson scores in severe haemophilia. Acta Radiol. 2002;43(5):528-532. https://doi.org/10.1034/j.1600-0455.2002.430514.x
Pettersson H, Ahlberg A, Nilsson IM. A radiologic classification of hemophilic arthropathy. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 1980;(149):153-159. PMID: 7408294.

pettersson_score.description: Conversion factor and cut-points used to represent cumulative radiographic joint damage. The 12.6 conversion is adopted directly from Zhou et al.; Fischer et al. independently reported approximately one Pettersson point per 13 joint bleeds.
reference: Direct source for conversion_factor 12.6: Zhou ZY et al. J Manag Care Spec Pharm. 2020;26(9):1109-1120. https://doi.org/10.18553/jmcp.2020.19406

Supporting empirical evidence (approximately 13 joint bleeds per Pettersson point; 295 radiographs from 117 patients): Fischer K et al. Acta Radiol. 2002;43(5):528-532. https://doi.org/10.1034/j.1600-0455.2002.430514.x

thresholds.description: Legacy Pettersson-score cut-points used by the model's three-band severity helper, plus its numerical cap. Utility assignment uses the more detailed evidence-defined bands in utilities.json.
reference: Zhou ZY et al. 2020 used Pettersson score >=1 for arthropathy, >=28 for orthopedic surgery, and score ranges 0-4, 5-27, and 28-78 for cost categories. https://doi.org/10.18553/jmcp.2020.19406
The original per-joint radiographic classification was defined by Pettersson H, Ahlberg A, and Nilsson IM. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 1980;(149):153-159. PMID: 7408294.
The stored maximum of 79 is an implementation cap; the published six-joint Pettersson scale has a maximum of 78.

treatment.description: Factor VIII dosing assumptions for prophylaxis and treatment of bleeding events.
treatment.reference: Srivastava A et al. WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition. https://doi.org/10.1111/hae.14046

dosing.description: Weekly prophylaxis and per-event doses in international units. ICH and aggregated non-ICH currently share a placeholder dose; test subtype-specific resource use in sensitivity analysis.
reference: Srivastava A et al. Haemophilia. 2020. https://doi.org/10.1111/hae.14046
Existing project dosing assumptions; regimen-specific derivation needs local clinical validation.

evidence.description: Published ABR evidence used to parameterize treatment-regime distributions.
evidence.reference: Each study estimate records its row-level source and DOI.

abr.description: Study-level ABR mean, dispersion, and sample-size inputs separated by treatment regime.
abr.reference: The source and doi fields on every estimate are its direct bibliographic reference.
